session.summary: The user discusses a project called 'Follow The Money' (FTFM), which aims to create a structured database of news and public statements to hold public figures accountable. The concept involves extracting entities and claims from media (initially Glenn Greenwald podcasts), tracking promises, identifying pattern changes in statements, and creating a searchable 'source of truth' system. The user also touches on technical implementation details including JSON structures, embeddings, and integration with Obsidian notes.

records.content: Create a proof of concept for Follow The Money (FTFM) by mapping entities and claims from Glenn Greenwald's podcasts over a six-month period. Extract all named entities, claims, and evidence, linking each to the exact moment when statements were made to create a verifiable 'source of truth'.

details.title: FTFM Proof of Concept Proposal
details.notes: Start with Glenn Greenwald's podcasts as initial dataset, then potentially expand to other media sources. Focus on creating a structured data model that captures statements and their context.

project.goal: Create a minimal viable proof of concept for the FTFM accountability system

records.content: Develop a system that automatically flags promises made by public figures and tracks future fulfillment. For example, when a politician says 'I will do X on my first day in office', the system records this claim and checks whether it was accomplished when the deadline arrives.

details.title: FTFM Promise Tracking System
details.notes: This feature would be particularly valuable for political campaigns and governance tracking. Will require temporal awareness and event correlation capabilities.

project.goal: Create an automated system for tracking and verifying public promises

records.content: Build a system that detects when public figures change their positions or contradict previous statements. This would create transparency around inconsistencies and enable citizens to easily verify how someone's stated positions have evolved over time.

details.title: FTFM Position Change Tracker
details.notes: Will require sophisticated natural language understanding to detect subtle shifts in position versus outright contradictions. Could implement a scoring system for consistency over time.

project.goal: Develop algorithms to identify and highlight changes in public positions over time

records.content: Implement a source credibility system that provides transparency about information quality. Sources could be weighted based on reliability metrics, with conflicts of interest documented and multiple perspectives available on controversial topics. This creates a system with variable truth weights while maintaining a single database structure.

details.title: FTFM Source Credibility Framework
details.notes: Will need to balance algorithmic weighting with user choice about which sources they trust. Could potentially integrate with existing fact-checking organizations.

project.goal: Create a transparent system for evaluating and displaying source credibility

records.content: Obtain transcripts from one or two Glenn Greenwald podcasts to use as initial test data for the FTFM model development.

details.title: Acquire Glenn Greenwald Podcast Transcripts
details.notes: Choose episodes that contain significant political claims or discussions of public figures to make the initial test meaningful. May need to use a transcription service if existing transcripts aren't available.

project.goal: Gather initial test data for FTFM entity extraction model

records.content: Design a technical architecture for FTFM with three main components: (1) A backend database of JSON structures with embedded metadata, (2) A translation layer that converts database records to markdown files and images, and (3) A frontend using Obsidian for viewing and editing notes with bidirectional syncing.

details.title: FTFM Technical Architecture Overview
details.notes: The bidirectional sync between backend database and Obsidian frontend will be particularly challenging but crucial for usability. Consider implementing a change detection system with conflict resolution.

project.goal: Define the complete technical stack and data flow for the FTFM system

records.content: Create a powerful RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system that can query the FTFM database to answer complex questions about public figures, events, and statements. The system should be able to synthesize information across multiple records and provide evidence-backed responses.

details.title: FTFM RAG Query System
details.notes: Use vector embeddings to enable semantic search across the database. Implementation should focus on evidence retrieval and citation to support all generated responses.

project.goal: Develop an AI-powered query system for the FTFM database

records.content: Maintain a daily journaling practice called 'Daily Story' that captures memorable moments in a single sentence. This is a lightweight alternative to full journaling that makes consistent documentation manageable.

details.title: Daily Story Journaling Practice
details.notes: Example entry mentioned: 'Today is cool with Ralphie and a memorable video call with Jaz.' Consider automating collection of these entries into weekly or monthly summaries.

area.responsibility: Maintain consistent documentation of daily experiences through single-sentence entries

records.content: Create an AI Dictation Project that can transform spoken ideas into structured data formats like JSON. This system would enable voice-directed research and content creation through natural language instructions.

details.title: AI Dictation and Research System
details.notes: This appears to be a separate project from FTFM but could potentially integrate with it. Voice interface for research tasks could dramatically accelerate information gathering.

project.goal: Build a voice-controlled AI system that can conduct research and structure information

records.content: The news needs a comprehensive 'storage layer' for day-to-day reality that goes beyond what Wikipedia provides. While Wikipedia offers static encyclopedic entries about important topics, we need a dynamic system that tracks ongoing events, statements, and changes in a structured, queryable format.

details.title: The Case for a News Storage Layer
details.notes: This philosophical foundation underpins the FTFM project and articulates why current systems (Wikipedia, traditional news) are insufficient for true accountability.

system_instructions.description: Create a single structured file containing all content from the transcript, organized into a coherent format
